Question: A 51-year-old man presents complaining of decreased vibratory sense in his lower limbs. Physical exam reveals a widened pulse pressure and a decrescendo murmur occurring after the S2 heart sound. After further questioning, he also reports he experienced a maculopapular rash over his trunk, palms and soles many years ago that resolved on its own. In order to evaluate the suspected diagnosis, the physician FIRST tested for which of the following?

Options:
opa. Agglutination of antibodies with beef cardiolipin
opb. Indirect immunofluoresence of the patient’s serum and killed T. palladium
opc. Cytoplasmic inclusions on Giemsa stain
opd. Agglutination of patients serum with Proteus O antigens
ope. Gram negative, oxidase positive, comma shaped bacteria growing at 42 degrees C
